target_customer: Engineering teams running coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex who pay for tokens and want spend governance
problem: Coding agents read large tool outputs such as logs, test runs and file trees, which burns tokens and money. Teams also lack visibility into agent spend across providers.
business_model: Usage-based credits (about 0.05 dollars per credit, Team plan 499 dollars per month, custom enterprise)
product_category: AI gateway and context compression for coding agents

founders.name: Michael Zhou
education: University of Toronto, BSc Computer Science and Neuroscience
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked on infrastructure at Okta and Shopify.

competitors.name: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
competitors.what: CLI proxy that compresses shell command output before it reaches the coding agent

technical_complexity.rationale: A local proxy that compresses tool outputs without hurting accuracy and fails open needs careful engineering, but is within reach of one strong engineer.

defensibility.rationale: Multiple open source and vendor tools compress tool output, and agent vendors can add their own truncation. A July 2026 study cited in search results questioned whether token reduction lowers billed cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Codex CLI already has a tool output token limit setting per search results, so vendors partly absorb the wedge. No further outcome is known.

market_need_then: Agent token bills were a visible pain in 2026, with many write-ups and tools on cutting coding agent token costs.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and technical, lowercase codag in product contexts, short declarative sentences

brand_strength.rationale: Short invented name with no found press about the brand. Third-party listings disagree on what the product does, which suggests little brand clarity so far.

outcome_analysis: Codag is a solo-founder Summer 2026 company and still active. It targets agent token cost, a real 2026 pain, but faces open source tools and vendor built-in limits. No exit, shutdown or layoff reports exist, so the outcome is open and depends on whether governance and analytics give it a paid edge over simple compression.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights alone lists 500 thousand dollars with Pioneer Fund and Y Combinator, a single aggregator, so no round is recorded. The product description on aggregators conflicts (log compression versus gateway). Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs.
